items.stem: Omitting a variable that affects both the regressor and the outcome causes what?

options.text: Omitted-variable bias in the estimated coefficient
options.rationale: Correct: a correlated omitted driver biases the coefficient.

options.text: Only a change in R-squared, with unbiased coefficients
options.rationale: The coefficient itself becomes biased, not just fit.
A correlated omitted variable does bias estimates.
That is a different problem entirely.

items.explanation: Correct: a correlated omitted driver biases the coefficient.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about regression results are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A statistically significant coefficient can still be practically trivial
options.rationale: Correct: significance does not imply a large or important effect.

options.text: A regression coefficient is not causal unless identification is credibly argued
options.rationale: Correct: association needs an identification strategy to be causal.

options.text: A high R-squared proves the model is correctly specified
options.rationale: High fit does not guarantee correct specification or causality.

options.text: A small p-value guarantees a large effect size
options.rationale: P-value and effect size are distinct.

items.explanation: Correct: significance does not imply a large or important effect.

items.stem: When errors are heteroskedastic but the model is otherwise well specified, what is an appropriate response?

options.text: Use robust (heteroskedasticity-consistent) standard errors for valid inference
options.rationale: Correct: robust errors fix inference under heteroskedasticity.

options.text: Ignore it because coefficients become biased anyway
options.rationale: Heteroskedasticity affects standard errors, not coefficient unbiasedness.

options.text: Drop half the data at random
options.rationale: That discards information and does not address the issue.

options.text: Switch to a causal claim without further work
options.rationale: Heteroskedasticity has nothing to do with establishing causation.

items.explanation: Correct: robust errors fix inference under heteroskedasticity.
